subject: Post-call: inference fit summary & JSON schema / retry playbook
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emma Zhang <emma.zhang@synthmed.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@synthmed.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Post-call: inference fit summary & JSON schema / retry playbook

Hi Emma / Liam,

Thanks again for the call today — great context on the clinical-extraction use case and the latency/cost targets. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we stay aligned.

TL;DR recommendations
- Model candidates: redwood-llama-70b-q4 (best quality/cost balance), llama-3-34b-quant (lower cost for high throughput), biomed-7b-ft (specialized entity extraction; smaller footprint).
- Eval scope: run a 3k-5k example pass across the three prompts we captured (attached prompt_sets_v1.jsonl) and collect token-level latency + exact-match/slot F1.
- Structured output: target JSON schema v1 (see summary below). We'll include schema validation in the eval harness; errors should be surfaced as structured diffs.
- Function/tool calling: use explicit function signatures for extraction + a small retry policy (idempotency token required). See details below.

JSON schema (summary)
- Top-level fields we expect: request_id, schema_version, patient_id, extracted_findings (array of objects).
- Each finding: { type, span_text, start_offset, end_offset, severity: [low|medium|high], confidence }.
- Validation approach: combine model-enforced structure (function call or structured output) with server-side JSON schema validator and a lightweight human-in-the-loop fallback for low-confidence items.

Function calling / retry guidance (short)
- Idempotency: include an idempotency_token header for every inference call so retries do not double-apply downstream side effects.
- Retry policy: retry on network/timeouts (5xx/gateway timeouts) with exponential backoff + full jitter; do NOT automatically retry on 4xx or model-level schema errors.
- Timeouts: recommend 8s per call for the larger models, 3s for the smaller 7b candidate when run on Dedicated.

Attachments included with this note:
- prompt_sets_v1.jsonl (3 prompt templates + expected slots)
- benchmark_inference_samples.csv (sample of tokens/latency we measured during call)


Next steps
1) Your team: confirm which prompts you want in scope (deadline: Tue 2027-08-17).
2) Redwood: we can run a pilot eval (3k examples) and deliver a results pack and failure-mode review by Fri 2027-08-27.
3) Karthik will follow up on pilot pricing and Dedicated trial capacity if you want a more controlled run.

If okay, I'll schedule the evaluation and share the Drive folder + HubSpot link for tracking.

Thanks,

--

Emma — great questions, answered inline below. Attaching a short sample set of past failure modes and a lightweight checklist.

1) "Always emit full structure" vs "partial outputs"
- Recommendation: prefer a model-emitted full structure (always include schema_version and request_id and top-level keys). This simplifies downstream consumers. If your production stack cannot rely on full structure from the model, the evaluator will normalize partial outputs, but that adds a second validation layer and increases complexity.

2) Header names & checklist for infra
- Header names we recommend: X-Redwood-Idempotency-Token, X-Redwood-Request-Id (optional), X-Client-Env (prod/stage/test).
- Checklist (short):
  - Confirm outbound header passthrough from your edge (we can test a sample request).
  - Verify timeouts at the edge: set request timeout >= model timeout + 500ms buffer.
  - Enforce idempotency token uniqueness per logical operation.
  - Log model responses and schema-validation errors to your audit stream.

3) Failure case examples (attached) — classification approach
- Syntactic failures: invalid JSON, missing commas, truncated arrays. These should be handled by immediate retries or model re-prompting.
- Schema violations: types wrong (string vs array) or missing required top-level fields; handled by server-side validation and a fallback extraction route.
- Semantic failures: model returns plausible but incorrect spans or wrong severity labels; these require eval-grade checks (gold labels) and confidence thresholds with human review for low-confidence items.

Pilot proposal (concrete)
- Redwood runs a 3k item pass across the three prompt templates (attached). Deliverables: per-model precision/recall/F1, latency distribution, top 50 failure cases with classifications, recommended schema-tightening changes.
- Estimated compute: ~30k token-requests; we can run on a Dedicated trial to ensure consistent latency.

Links and artifacts
- Drive playbook: https://drive.google.com/synthmed/inference-fit-playbook
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/SYNTH-2027-08

I attached a bundle: sample-failures.csv and the checklist. If you want we can also include a short demo of the schema validator in action (recorded screen + logs).

I'll coordinate with Karthik on pricing for the pilot if you give the green light.

Best,
